title: BPP act_intent_position request (DESIGN.md §13.1, §10.3, §14.8; registry R20 participant / R21 governance)
description: Mutation (meta required). Fills only the authenticated actor's exact prepared seat on the exact prepared ActIntent: proposal_ref/proposal_revision name the prepared intent and subject_digest is its exact digest (R20/R21 fence: exact intent digest). Dual-surface operation — one schema pair per operation, surface is a registry key the schema cannot express (gap note G35): a Participant fills its exact prepared participant/resource-owner seat on the participant surface (R20); a human principal fills its exact prepared human-authority seat on the governance surface with a fresh challenge as required (R21). position_id, revision, participant_ref, actor_ref, participant_binding_epoch, endpoint_incarnation, recovery_epoch, authentication_observation_ref, status, and digest are server-derived (§10.3, §14.3). Withdraw/supersede is seat-head CAS via prior_position_digest plus target_status — gap note G18. Stage-capable (R20/R21).

proposal_ref.description: The prepared ActIntent (§10.3 Position field names kept verbatim — gap note G35).

subject_digest.description: The exact prepared intent digest (R20/R21 fence).

seat_ref.description: The authenticated actor's own prepared seat only (§14.6); another actor's seat fails position_ineligible.

prior_position_digest.description: Seat-head CAS when superseding or withdrawing a prior revision (§10.3).

target_status.description: Pre-finalization withdraw encoding; absent means active (gap note G18).

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with Z offset, semantically valid in the proleptic Gregorian calendar: the pattern pins the lexical ranges and implementations MUST additionally reject impossible calendar instants (e.g. 2026-02-30) — the conformance runner enforces this on every vector; leap seconds are not accepted. DESIGN.md does not fix a timestamp wire encoding; this derivation freezes with the bundle (gap note G3, amended per RT-17).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef: every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Wire shape, class/algorithm pairing, and key_ref presence per the ratified family profile.

mutationMeta.description: MutationMeta (§14.2), create-classed: this operation creates a record (or CASes a subordinate head through its own body fields), so the closed create meta carries NO expected_revision member — supplying one fails the closed schema (RT-01: update CAS is structural, never optional).

localErasureSafeDigest.description: Contextual digest-class binding (PROFILE.md §6.2, D-R0-1; RT-02): this field commits to an authority subject or other erasable per-object content, so exactly class local_erasure_safe (per-object secret, keyed HMAC) is acceptable. A well-constructed digest of any other class here is digest_class_mismatch — never a silent substitution.
